title: Stakeholder orchestration playbook for high-risk rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an orchestration playbook that codifies stakeholder responsibilities, escalation ladders, and pre-authorized rollback triggers for releases that materially change inference behavior (latency, quantization, KV cache semantics) or console control planes. This doc ties together release notes cadence, cross-team signoffs, incident comms templates, and a dry-run checklist to reduce ambiguity during launches.
background: We have observed ambiguous ownership during previous high-impact launches where runtime and console changes rolled out in different waves. That led to delayed rollbacks and inconsistent external comms. This initiative consolidates a single source of truth for who calls a rollback, what customer-facing messaging looks like, and how to coordinate partner and legal notifications.
scope: Applies to hosted API releases and Dedicated/Private deployment changes that affect API surface (structured output changes), model routing policies, or autoscaling defaults. Excludes purely documentation-only edits and routine SDK patch releases.
success_criteria: Pre-approved rollback decision matrix exists and is signed-off by Eng, Security, Support, and GTM
One-click contact list (paging order) is available in the console for on-call leads
Two dry-run exercises completed with < 15 minute decision time for simulated outage
Release notes sent to top 20 customers and partner channel within 2 hours of GA
Post-release survey metric: Support volume spike < 30% above baseline for similar launches
owner_matrix: Rollback decision authority: Product (Aisha) + Runtime Eng Lead (Priya) - both must agree
Oncall execution: SRE (Tanya) executes rollback scripts after decision
Release notes coordination: PM (Aisha) drafts, Docs (Monica Li) edits, GTM (Elena) distributes
Monitoring & metrics owners: Runtime (Priya) for token-level errors, Console (Marco) for UI/UX regressions
orchestrated_checklist: T-14d: Complete security_review_required checklist and KMS/HSM signoff
T-10d: Draft release notes and hot-path customer FAQ; distribute to Customer Success for review
T-7d: Conduct cross-team readiness meeting (Runtime, Console, SRE, Support, Legal, GTM)
T-3d: Run dry-run 1 (simulated partial degradation) with real paging flow; document time-to-decision
T-1d: Lock release candidate; publish 'go/no-go' dashboard and final contact list
T+0 (hour 0): Confirm observability alerts active, enable higher-fidelity sampling for impacted routes
T+1h: GTM sends initial customer note to top customers if GA ship is confirmed
T+2h: Publish release notes on docs site, send to all API users via newsletter and product status feed
T+24h: Collect support volume change and automatic regression checks; if thresholds exceeded, trigger review
rollback_plan: Pre-reqs: Tested rollback playbook in staging; rollback scripts in private repo with access controlled by SRE
Trigger conditions: sustained token error rate > 5% above baseline for 10 minutes OR latency 2x SLO for 5 minutes on 99th percentile
Decision path: PM + Runtime Eng Lead must agree; if disagreement, escalate to CTO (Marcus Yi) who has tiebreak authority
Rollback steps: (1) Switch traffic to previous model variant via routing policy (smart routing fallback); (2) Revert console feature flag; (3) Notify SSO/KMS teams if secrets rotated
Post-rollback: run smoke tests, open bi-directional status Slack channel, and prepare customer-facing incident note within 60 minutes
incident_comm_templates: Initial internal page (Slack #release-ops): 'Incident: [short id] — Observed elevated errors on runtime route /v1/generate. Triage ongoing. PM: Aisha, SRE: Tanya. Join #incident-[short id] for updates.'

External short notice (top customers): 'We are experiencing elevated errors affecting text-generation latency for some requests. Our engineers are investigating; we will provide updates within 30 minutes. If you are experiencing a critical outage, contact your CSM or reply to this message.'

Post-rollback public incident note (status page): 'Resolved — We rolled back to the previous model variant at 15:42 UTC due to increased error rates. A restoration was performed and service health is green. We are investigating root cause and will post a follow-up.'

Support canned reply: 'Hi — thanks for reporting. We observed a service degradation earlier; we have rolled back and are monitoring. Please let us know if you still see issues and include request IDs if available.'
release_notes_instructions: Structure: TL;DR, What changed (user-facing), Why we changed it, Migration or compatibility notes, Known regressions/fixes, Contact links
Localization: Provide short localized TL;DR for EU/APAC customers where the change affects latency or privacy controls
Embargo policy: Do not publish until T+2h unless an immediate customer note is required by PM
Changelog automation: Use the release-notes-generator GH action; link PRs in the final published notes
coordination_cadence: Cadence: Daily stand in at T-7d..T-1d, then hourly sync during T+0..T+6h. Use #release-ops for async updates; incidents escalate to #incidents and the rotation oncall.
dry_run_plan: Dry-run 1 (partial degradation scenario): simulate elevated latency on a small routing shard; validate decision loop and rollback time < 20 minutes
Dry-run 2 (control-plane regression): flip console feature flag in staging and verify customer-visible doc generation and release notes flow
Post-dry-run retro: capture gaps in contact lists, missing runbook steps, and any GitHub repo access errors
